name: lr_abort
description: Stops script execution: the Actions section is aborted, the vuser_end section still runs, and the run ends with a "Stopped" status. Use it to stop a script manually when a specific error condition occurs. Equivalent to lr_exit(LR_EXIT_VUSER, LR_ABORT). Returns no value.

name: lr_advance_param
description: Advances the parameter to the next available value in the parameter data file, so the script uses a new value in the middle of an iteration. Complements the automatic "Select next row" setting in the parameter properties; this function is not recorded automatically and must be inserted manually. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

args.name: param
args.desc: Parameter name in quotation marks (without curly braces).

name: lr_aws_get_secret
description: Retrieves a secret from AWS Secrets Manager and stores it in a parameter. All string arguments support standard parameterization. Returns 0 on success and 1 on error.

args.name: ServerUrl
args.desc: URL for the web request to the AWS service.

args.name: AccessKey
args.desc: Access key used to authenticate to the AWS service.

args.name: SecretKey
args.desc: Secret key used to authenticate to the AWS service.

args.name: SecretId
args.desc: ARN or name of the secret to retrieve.

args.name: ResultParamName
args.desc: Name of the parameter in which the retrieved secret is stored.

example:
lr_aws_get_secret(
    "ServerUrl=https://secretsmanager.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/",
    "AccessKey=ABCDE3F5VDXCR23GV",
    "SecretKey=Sfp01wlur0zsVoOKuMTuDV9fpkDdxdHrJuK0",
    "SecretId=arn:aws:secretsmanager:eu-central-1:2345653738:secret:lrp-web-protocol-secret-paRino",
    "ResultParamName=TEST",
    LAST);

name: lr_azure_ad_client_get_token
description: Retrieves a bearer token from the Azure API service using client credentials. The token can be used in subsequent Azure operations, for example retrieving a secret from Key Vault. Returns 0 on success and 1 on error.

args.name: ResultParamName
args.desc: Name of the parameter in which the token is stored.

args.name: TenantID
args.desc: Azure Active Directory tenant ID.

args.name: ClientID
args.desc: ID of the application registered in Azure Active Directory.

args.name: ClientSecret
args.desc: Client secret used for authentication.

example:
rc = lr_azure_ad_client_get_token("ResultParamName=token1",
                                  "TenantID=xxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxx",
                                  "ClientID=xxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxxxxx",
                                  "ClientSecret=xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx", LAST);

name: lr_azure_kv_get_secret
description: Retrieves a secret value from Microsoft Azure Key Vault based on the vault URL and secret name. Requires an authentication token obtained separately (for example with lr_azure_ad_client_get_token). All string arguments support standard parameterization. Returns 0 on success and 1 on error.

args.name: ResultParamName
args.desc: Name of the parameter in which the secret is stored.

args.name: VaultURL
args.desc: URL Azure Key Vault.

args.name: SecretName
args.desc: Name of the secret to retrieve.

args.name: SecretVersion
args.desc: Optional. Secret version; if omitted, the latest version is retrieved.

args.name: Token
args.desc: Authentication token.

name: lr_azure_set_service_port
description: Sets the port used to connect to the local Azure API service. Returns 0 on success and 1 on error.

args.name: portNum
args.desc: Port number for the connection to the local Azure API service (default 16888).

name: lr_checkpoint
description: Validates a parameter value against an expected value (checkpoint). If validation fails, the script stops or continues depending on StopOnValidationError and the Continue on Error runtime setting. Windows only, case-sensitive, and must be added manually. Returns LR_PASS on success and LR_FAIL on failure.

args.name: StepName
args.desc: Step name as displayed in the test tree.

args.name: ActualValue
args.desc: Data to compare with ExpectedValue (a value or a parameter).

args.name: Compare
args.desc: Comparison operator: Equals, NotEquals, Contains, StartsWith, EndsWith.

args.name: ExpectedValue
args.desc: Reference data that ActualValue is compared against (a value or a parameter).

args.name: StopOnValidationError
args.desc: Boolean: true = fail/stop; false = continue.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_continue_on_error
description: Specifies how runtime errors are handled in a specific script segment, that is, whether execution continues or stops on error. Overrides the default Continue on Error setting in Runtime Settings only for the enclosed section. Returns no value.

args.name: value
args.desc: Error continuation option (for example 1 = continue on error, 0 = disabled).

name: lr_convert_double_to_double
description: Reformats the string representation of a double value using a printf-style format specifier and stores the result in the target parameter. Output is limited to 63 characters. If the input is not purely numeric, valid leading characters are still converted (for example "1234ABCDF" becomes 1234), while a string that does not start with a numeric character causes an error. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success and LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: source_param_name
args.desc: Name of the parameter containing the double value to reformat.

args.name: format_string
args.desc: printf-style format specifier for the output.

args.name: target_param_name
args.desc: Name of the parameter that stores the formatted string.

name: lr_convert_double_to_integer
description: Converts a double value string to an integer string by discarding the fractional part. The target parameter is created automatically if it does not exist. Leading numeric characters are still converted ("1234ABCDF" becomes 1234); a string that does not start with a digit causes an error. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success and LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: source_param_name
args.desc: Name of the parameter containing the double value to convert.

args.name: target_param_name
args.desc: Name of the parameter that stores the integer result.

name: lr_convert_string_encoding
description: Converts the encoding of a string between System locale, Unicode, and UTF-8. The result (including the NULL terminator) is stored in the paramName parameter; printable characters appear as-is in the log, while non-printable characters appear in hexadecimal. Must be added manually. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

args.name: sourceString
args.desc: String to convert.

args.name: fromEncoding
args.desc: Encoding of sourceString (for example LR_ENC_SYSTEM_LOCALE).

args.name: toEncoding
args.desc: Target encoding (for example LR_ENC_UNICODE, LR_ENC_UTF8).

args.name: paramName
args.desc: Name of the parameter in which the resulting string is stored.

name: lr_cyberark_get_vault
description: Retrieves a protected password from a CyberArk Vault and Safe and stores it in a parameter. The certificate and private key must be in PEM format. All string arguments support parameterization. Returns 0 on success and 1 on error.

args.name: ServerUrl
args.desc: URL for the web request.

args.name: CertPath
args.desc: Path to the certificate.

args.name: KeyPath
args.desc: Optional. Path to the private key.

args.name: Password
args.desc: Optional. Password for the private key.

args.name: AppID
args.desc: Application ID used in the web request.

args.name: Safe
args.desc: CyberArk Safe in which the application resides.

args.name: AccountName
args.desc: Name of the account object in the safe.

args.name: ExtraQueryData
args.desc: Optional. Additional query data in key=value format.

args.name: ResultParamName
args.desc: Name of the parameter in which the retrieved password is stored.

example:
lr_cyberark_get_vault(
       "ServerUrl=https://test.skytap.com/AIMWebService/api/Accounts",
       "CertPath=D:\\feature\\cyberark\\Certs needed to make CCP call\\client_1-28.crt",
        "KeyPath=D:\\feature\\cyberark\\Certs needed to make CCP call\\client.pem",
        "Password=Cyberark1",
        "AppID=testappid",
        "Safe=Test",
        "AccountName=testobject1",
        "ResultParamName=TEST",
        LAST);

name: lr_db_connect
description: Creates a database connection used by other database functions such as lr_db_executeSQLStatement. Runs on Windows only and should be placed in vuser_init to minimize overhead. For Oracle, use the OLEDB ConnectionType. Always returns zero.

args.name: StepName
args.desc: Step name as displayed in the test tree; free text.

args.name: ConnectionString
args.desc: Database connection details; the syntax depends on the data provider.

args.name: ConnectionName
args.desc: Logical identifier for the connection.

args.name: ConnectionType
args.desc: Data provider type: SQL, OLEDB, ODBC, or ORACLE.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

example:
lr_db_connect("StepName=DatabaseConnection",
        "ConnectionString=Data Source=myServer.myLab.ad;Initial Catalog=InvDatabase;Persist Security Info=True;User ID=myUser;Password=myPassword",
        "ConnectionName=InvDatabaseConnection",
        "ConnectionType=SQL",
        LAST );

name: lr_db_dataset_action
description: Performs an action on a dataset: resets the cursor to the first record, frees memory, or prints the dataset to the Replay Log. When printing, only the first 100 records are shown in the report summary. Windows only; string arguments support parameterization. Returns LR_PASS on success and LR_FAIL on failure.

args.name: StepName
args.desc: Step name as displayed in the test tree; free text.

args.name: DatasetName
args.desc: Logical name of the dataset defined in lr_db_executeSQLStatement.

args.name: Action
args.desc: RESET (move the cursor to the first record), REMOVE (free memory), or PRINT (print to the Replay Log).

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_db_disconnect
description: Closes a database connection created with lr_db_connect. Windows only; must be called once for each active connection and should be placed in vuser_end rather than in an Action. Returns LR_PASS on success and LR_FAIL on failure.

args.name: StepName
args.desc: Step name as displayed in the test tree; free text.

args.name: ConnectionName
args.desc: Logical name of the connection defined in lr_db_connect.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

example:
lr_db_disconnect("StepName=Disconnect",
        "ConnectionName=db1", LAST );

name: lr_db_executeSQLStatement
description: Sends an SQL statement to the database (Windows only). Returns the number of records in the dataset (excluding the header row) on success, or LR_FAIL on failure. After the call, the cursor row is undefined, so set Row to next or 1 when calling lr_db_getValue.

args.name: StepName
args.desc: Step name as displayed in the test tree; free text.

args.name: ConnectionName
args.desc: Logical name of the database connection from lr_db_connect.

args.name: SQLStatement
args.desc: SQL statement (SELECT, INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE); the syntax depends on the database; supports parameterization.

args.name: DatasetName
args.desc: Logical name of the dataset holding the SELECT query results; used for SELECT only.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_db_getValue
description: Retrieves a value from a dataset created by lr_db_executeSQLStatement, with options for positioning the row cursor. Automatically wraps back to the first record after reaching the end; binary data is displayed as <binary_data>. Windows only. Returns LR_PASS on success, LR_FAIL on failure, and -1 when the cursor reaches the last record or on the first call.

args.name: StepName
args.desc: Step name as displayed in the test tree.

args.name: DatasetName
args.desc: Logical name of the dataset defined in lr_db_executeSQLStatement.

args.name: Column
args.desc: Name of the dataset column whose value is retrieved.

args.name: Row
args.desc: Cursor position: a row number (starting at 1), current (do not move), or next (advance to the next row).

args.name: OutParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter that receives the result value.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_debug_message
description: Sends a debug message to the log file only if the specified message class is currently enabled (through Runtime Settings or lr_set_debug_message). The message appears in the output window when Expert Mode and debug information are enabled. Returns the number of characters written (excluding the null terminator), or a negative value on error.

args.name: message_level
args.desc: One of the Runtime Settings log message classes (Disabled does not apply), for example LR_MSG_CLASS_EXTENDED_LOG.

args.name: format
args.desc: printf-style format string, followed by optional arguments.

name: lr_decrypt
description: Decodes (unmasks) an encoded string during replay; VuGen records the original password but displays the encoded version inside lr_decrypt. This function is deprecated; use lr_unmask. Returns a pointer to the decoded string, or NULL on error.

args.name: EncodedString
args.desc: Encoded string to decode.

name: lr_decrypt_ex
description: Decrypts a message encrypted with lr_encrypt_ex. The AES key must be configured first. The ciphertext argument supports parameterization. Returns the decrypted string.

args.name: ciphertext
args.desc: Encrypted string to decrypt.

name: lr_disable_ip_spoofing
description: Disables IP spoofing during script execution. Paired with lr_enable_ip_spoofing. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

name: lr_enable_ip_spoofing
description: Enables IP spoofing during script execution, so that Vusers can use different IP addresses. Paired with lr_disable_ip_spoofing. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

name: lr_encrypt_ex
description: Encrypts a message using the AES-256-GCM algorithm (FIPS compliant). The result can be decrypted with lr_decrypt_ex. The AES key must be configured first. Returns the encrypted string.

args.name: plaintext
args.desc: String to encrypt.

name: lr_end_cross_vuser_transaction
description: Marks the completion of a transaction started by another Vuser (cross-Vuser transaction), from the perspective of the receiving Vuser. The script logic determines when the transaction ends and its status. If the ID parameter value is longer than 16 bytes or contains a null character, it is replaced with an MD5 hash. Not recorded automatically and does not support standard parameterization. Returns zero on success, -1 on failure, or TRANSACTION_MSGS_EMPTY_START_TRANSACTION_STRING / TRANSACTION_MSGS_EMPTY_IDENTIFIER_DATA for empty arguments.

args.name: transaction_name
args.desc: Name of the cross-Vuser transaction.

args.name: trans_id_param
args.desc: Parameter containing the transaction ID string; must match the value used by the starting Vuser in lr_start_cross_vuser_transaction.

args.name: status
args.desc: Completion status: LR_PASS, LR_FAIL, LR_AUTO, LR_ABORT, LR_STOP, LR_TIMED_OUT, or LR_USER_DEFINED.

name: lr_end_sub_transaction
description: Marks the end of a sub-transaction. Must be paired with lr_start_sub_transaction; sub-transactions can be nested inside a parent transaction, but each end must have a matching start or an error occurs. Arguments do not support standard parameterization. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the name is invalid or there is no matching lr_start_sub_transaction.

args.name: sub_transaction
args.desc: Name string of an existing sub-transaction.

args.name: status
args.desc: Transaction status (LR_PASS, LR_FAIL, LR_AUTO, etc.).

name: lr_end_transaction
description: Marks the end of a transaction and records its execution time; paired with lr_start_transaction. The status can be set manually (LR_PASS, LR_FAIL, LR_STOP) or automatically with LR_AUTO, which uses LR_PASS unless changed by a status-setting function. Returns 0 on success and -1 if the transaction name is invalid or there is no matching lr_start_transaction.

args.name: transaction_name
args.desc: Name string of an existing transaction.

args.name: status
args.desc: Transaction status value: LR_PASS, LR_FAIL, LR_STOP, or LR_AUTO.

name: lr_end_transaction_instance
description: Ends a transaction instance and records the elapsed time; paired with lr_start_transaction_instance. The status can be set manually or automatically with LR_AUTO. Returns 0 on success and a negative number on failure.

args.name: parent_handle
args.desc: Handle returned by lr_start_transaction_instance when the instance was created.

args.name: status
args.desc: Transaction status: LR_PASS, LR_FAIL, LR_STOP, or LR_AUTO.

name: lr_end_timer
description: Stops a timer started by lr_start_timer and returns its duration in seconds, with up to microsecond precision depending on the runtime environment.

args.name: timer
args.desc: Timer handle returned by lr_start_timer.

name: lr_error_message
description: Sends an error message to the output window, the log file, and the test report summary, together with location information. The message is limited to 5 KB. If the runtime setting "Fail open transactions on lr_error_message" is enabled, calling this function also fails any open transactions. Returns the message length on success, or a negative number on failure.

args.name: format
args.desc: Format string sent to the Output window; a quoted literal or a standard message format.

args.name: exp1, exp2,..expn
args.desc: Expressions/variables to format.

name: lr_eval_json
description: Parses JSON content, creates a JSON object, and stores its handle in a parameter. The input can be a string or a file. Only ANSI and UTF-8 encodings are supported; not recorded automatically. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

args.name: Buffer
args.desc: String JSON.

args.name: Buffer/File
args.desc: Path of the file containing the JSON string.

args.name: JsonObject
args.desc: Name of the parameter that stores the JSON object handle.

name: lr_eval_string
description: Returns the argument string after all parameters in it (enclosed in curly braces) have been evaluated. Memory is freed automatically at the end of each iteration. If the string contains only a single parameter, the function returns that parameter's value; returns NULL if evaluation fails.

args.name: instring
args.desc: String to evaluate; parameters are written in curly braces, for example {name}.

name: lr_eval_string_ext
signature: int lr_eval_string_ext( const char *in_string, unsigned long const in_len, char ** const out_str, unsigned long * const out_len, unsigned long const options, const char *file, long const line );
description: Evaluates a string by replacing parameters with their values, then allocates a buffer containing the result. Designed for binary data, including strings with embedded NULL characters. The buffer must be freed with lr_eval_string_ext_free. Preferable to lr_eval_string when processing in loops, to save memory. Returns LR_PASS (0) on success and LR_FAIL (1) on failure.

args.name: in_str
args.desc: String to evaluate.

args.name: in_len
args.desc: Length of the argument name plus 2 (for the curly braces).

args.name: out_str
args.desc: Pointer to the output buffer.

args.name: out_len
args.desc: Length of the output buffer.

args.name: options
args.desc: Reserved for future use; set to 0.

args.name: file
args.desc: Reserved for future use; set to 0.

args.name: line
args.desc: Reserved for future use; set to -1.

name: lr_eval_string_ext_free
description: Frees memory allocated by lr_eval_string_ext. Call it once you have finished with the buffer to prevent memory leaks. Returns no value.

args.name: param
args.desc: Pointer to the buffer to free.

name: lr_exit
description: Exits the script, action, or iteration during a run. Transactions that contain lr_exit do not appear in the Controller's Transaction Status box and are not counted as pass/fail. If called multiple times, the exit status of the last call determines the final status of the Vuser group. lr_exit(LR_EXIT_VUSER, LR_ABORT) is equivalent to lr_abort. Returns no value.

args.name: continuation_option
args.desc: How the script continues after lr_exit (for example LR_EXIT_VUSER, LR_EXIT_ACTION_AND_CONTINUE, LR_EXIT_ITERATION_AND_CONTINUE).

args.name: exit_status
args.desc: Exit status of the scenario group resulting from this call (for example LR_PASS, LR_FAIL, LR_AUTO, LR_ABORT).

name: lr_fail_trans_with_error
description: Sets LR_FAIL as the default result of all open transactions that use LR_AUTO in lr_end_transaction, and sends an error message to the output window or log. By default, an LR_AUTO transaction resolves to LR_PASS. Arguments do not support standard parameterization. Returns the message length on success and a negative number on failure.

args.name: format
args.desc: printf-style format string for the message.

args.name: exp1, exp2,.. expn
args.desc: Optional. Expressions/variables to format and print.

name: lr_free_parameter
description: Deletes a dynamic parameter at runtime and frees its buffer memory, for example a parameter created by web_reg_save_param or lr_save_string. Important for managing memory consumption. Arguments do not support standard parameterization. Returns 0 on success, or a negative number if the parameter is not found or deallocation fails.

args.name: param
args.desc: Name of the dynamic parameter to free.

name: lr_get_attrib_double
description: Retrieves the value of a double-type argument supplied when running the script (a command-line argument). Arguments can be viewed in the mdrv_cmd.txt file in the script folder. Does not support standard parameterization. Returns the double value on success, or -1 if the argument does not exist or its value is not compatible with the double type (for example a flag parameter).

args.name: argument_name
args.desc: Name of an argument that can be interpreted as a double value.

name: lr_get_attrib_long
description: Retrieves the value of a long-integer argument supplied when running the script. Arguments can be viewed in the mdrv_cmd.txt file in the script folder. Does not support standard parameterization. Returns the long value on success, or -1 if the argument does not exist or cannot be interpreted as a long.

args.name: argument_name
args.desc: Name of an argument that can be interpreted as a long integer.

name: lr_get_attrib_string
description: Retrieves the value of a script command-line argument as a string. If the argument is empty, an empty string is returned; if the argument does not exist, NULL is returned.

args.name: argument_name
args.desc: Name of the script invocation argument.

name: lr_get_debug_message
description: Returns the current message logging setting (from runtime settings or lr_set_debug_message) as an unsigned integer. A base value of 0, 1, or 16 indicates Disabled, Brief, or Extended Log; additional flags (2, 4, 8, 512) can be OR-ed with Extended Log for Result Data, Parameter Substitution, Full Runtime Trace, or error-only. Use a bitwise AND operation to check the options.

name: lr_get_host_name
description: Returns the name of the host machine running the script. The returned value points to static data and must be read only, not modified. Returns NULL on failure.

name: lr_get_master_host_name
description: Returns the name of the machine running the Controller. The returned value points to static data and must be read only. Returns NULL on failure.
example:
char * controller_host;
controller_host = lr_get_master_host_name( );

name: lr_get_transaction_duration
description: Retrieves the running duration, in seconds, of a still-open transaction by name. The value includes wasted time, so it can be slightly larger than the final duration recorded by lr_end_transaction. Returns a positive value only for open transactions; returns 0 if the transaction has already ended or data is unavailable, and a negative number on failure.

args.name: transaction
args.desc: Transaction name string.

name: lr_get_transaction_status
description: Retrieves the current status of a still-open transaction. Cannot be called after lr_end_transaction and does not report the final status. Useful in multi-step transactions so that a Vuser can stop early once it has failed. If Continue on Error is disabled, the check after an error may not be reached. Returns the transaction status value, or a negative number on error.

args.name: transaction
args.desc: Transaction name string.

name: lr_get_trans_instance_duration
description: Retrieves the running duration, in seconds, of a still-open transaction instance by its handle. Unlike lr_get_transaction_duration, which uses the name. Returns a value greater than zero only for open transactions; 0 if the instance has already ended or data is unavailable, and a negative value on failure.

args.name: trans_handle
args.desc: Transaction handle (the return value of lr_start_transaction_instance).

name: lr_get_trans_instance_status
description: Retrieves the current status of an active transaction instance. Cannot be called after the transaction has ended and does not report the final status. Useful for monitoring multi-step transactions that can fail at various points. Returns the transaction instance status, or a negative number on error.

args.name: transaction_handle
args.desc: Transaction instance handle returned by lr_start_transaction_instance.

name: lr_get_trans_instance_think_time
description: Retrieves the think time of a transaction instance by its handle. Returns a value greater than zero only for open transactions; 0 if the instance has already ended or data is unavailable, and a negative value on failure.

args.name: trans_handle
args.desc: Transaction handle returned by lr_start_transaction_instance().

name: lr_get_trans_instance_wasted_time
description: Retrieves the wasted time, in seconds, of a transaction instance by its handle. Returns a value greater than zero only for open transactions; 0 if the instance has already ended or data is unavailable, and a negative value on failure.

args.name: trans_handle
args.desc: Transaction handle returned by lr_start_transaction_instance.

name: lr_get_transaction_think_time
description: Retrieves the think time accumulated in an open transaction up to the current execution point, by transaction name. Returns a positive value only for transactions still running; 0 if the transaction has already ended or data is unavailable, and a negative value on failure.

args.name: transaction
args.desc: Transaction name.

name: lr_get_transaction_wasted_time
description: Retrieves the wasted time, in seconds, accumulated in an open transaction up to the current execution point. Meaningful only for transactions that are still active; returns 0 if the transaction has already ended or data is unavailable, and a negative number on failure.

args.name: transaction
args.desc: Name of the transaction to query.

name: lr_get_vuser_ip
description: Retrieves the IPv4 address currently assigned to the Vuser when IP spoofing is enabled, for example when the IP is set through web_set_sockets_option with the IP_ADDRESS_BY_INDEX option. For an IPv6 address, use lr_get_attrib_string("ipv6"). Returns a pointer to the IP string, or NULL on failure or if IP spoofing is disabled.

name: lr_json_delete
description: Deletes values in a JSON object that match a query. Not recorded automatically and must be inserted manually. Supports deleting one or many matches, with configurable error handling. Returns the number of items deleted.

args.name: JsonObject
args.desc: Name of the JSON object parameter created with lr_eval_json.

args.name: QueryString
args.desc: JSON query that matches the items to delete.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: Optional. Yes deletes all matches; No deletes only the first (default No).

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Optional. Error stops the script; Continue only issues a warning (default Error).

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_json_find
signature: int lr_json_find( "JsonObject=<parameter name>", "Value or ValueParam=<value>", "QueryString=<query>", ["SelectAll=<Yes|No>",] ["IgnoreCase=<Yes|No>",] ["UseRegExp=<Yes|No>",] ["NotFound=<Error|Continue>",] LAST);
description: Runs a query on a JSON object and returns the number of results that match the searched value. Supports regular expression filtering, case-insensitive matching, and error handling when nothing is found. When SelectAll=No, the return value is only 0 or 1.

args.name: JsonObject
args.desc: Name of the parameter that holds the JSON object handle returned by lr_eval_json.

args.name: QueryString
args.desc: JSON query to run.

args.name: Value
args.desc: Value to search for.

args.name: ValueParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter containing the value to search for.

args.name: UseRegExp
args.desc: Optional. Yes treats Value as a regular expression (default No).

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: Optional. Yes returns the total number of matches; No stops at the first (default No).

args.name: IgnoreCase
args.desc: Optional. Yes ignores case differences (default No).

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Optional. Error stops the script (default); Continue only issues a warning.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_json_get_values
signature: int lr_json_get_values( "JsonObject=<parameter name>", "ValueParam=<parameter name>", "QueryString=<JSON query>", ["SelectAll=<Yes|No>",] ["NotFound=<Error|Continue>",] LAST );
description: Retrieves data from JSON object nodes that match a query and stores it in the ValueParam parameter. Not recorded automatically and must be inserted manually. Returns the number of matching nodes.

args.name: JsonObject
args.desc: Name of the parameter that holds the JSON object handle returned by lr_eval_json.

args.name: ValueParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter in which the retrieved data is stored.

args.name: QueryString
args.desc: JSON query/path.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: Optional. Yes retrieves all matches; No stops at the first (default No).

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Optional. Error stops the script; Continue only issues a warning (default Error).

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_json_insert
signature: int lr_json_insert( "JsonObject=<parameter name>", "Value or ValueParam or JsonNode=<value>", "QueryString=<query>", ["SelectAll=<Yes|No>",] ["NotFound=<Error|Continue>",] LAST );
description: Inserts a value into a JSON object at the location specified by a query. Can insert a string, a value from a parameter, or an entire JSON object node, optionally at all matching locations. Returns the number of matches at insertion.

args.name: JsonObject
args.desc: Name of the parameter that holds the JSON object handle returned by lr_eval_json.

args.name: QueryString
args.desc: JSON path where the node is inserted.

args.name: Value
args.desc: String to insert; it must be parseable as a JSON array/object matching the target type.

args.name: ValueParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter containing the string to insert.

args.name: JsonNode
args.desc: Parameter containing the handle of the JSON object to insert into JsonObject.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: Optional (default No). Yes inserts at all matching locations; No only at the first.

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Optional (default Error). Error stops the script; Continue issues a warning and proceeds.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_json_replace
signature: int lr_json_replace("JsonObject=<parameter name>", "Value or ValueParam or JsonNode=<value>", "QueryString=<query>", ["SelectAll=<Yes|No>",] ["NotFound=<Error|Continue>",] LAST);
description: Replaces the node identified by a query in a JSON object with a new key-value pair. Unlike lr_json_set_values, this function changes both the key and the value. If several pairs are supplied, only the first pair is used. Returns the number of matches replaced.

args.name: JsonObject
args.desc: Name of the parameter that holds the JSON object handle returned by lr_eval_json.

args.name: QueryString
args.desc: JSON path that identifies the node to replace.

args.name: Value
args.desc: Replacement key-value pair for the matching node; curly braces are optional.

args.name: ValueParam
args.desc: Parameter containing the replacement key-value pair.

args.name: JsonNode
args.desc: Parameter containing the handle of the JSON object that replaces the query result.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: Optional (default No). Yes replaces all matches; No only the first.

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Optional (default Error). Error stops the script; Continue issues a warning.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_json_set_values
signature: int lr_json_set_values( "JsonObject=<parameter name>", "Value or ValueParam=<value>", "QueryString=<query>", ["SelectAll=<Yes|No>",] ["NotFound=<Error|Continue>",] LAST );
description: Changes the value of JSON object nodes that match a query. When using a parameter array with SelectAll=Yes, each array element replaces the matches in order. To change the key name as well as the value, use lr_json_replace. Returns the number of nodes updated.

args.name: JsonObject
args.desc: Parameter that holds the JSON object handle from lr_eval_json.

args.name: QueryString
args.desc: JSON path/query.

args.name: Value
args.desc: Data to set on the matching nodes.

args.name: ValueParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter containing the data; with SelectAll=Yes, supply an array with as many elements as there are matches.

args.name: SelectAll
args.desc: Optional (default No). Yes updates all matches; No stops at the first.

args.name: NotFound
args.desc: Optional (default Error). Error stops the script; Continue issues a warning.

args.name: LAST
args.desc: Marks the end of the argument list.

name: lr_json_stringify
description: Converts a JSON object to a JSON string without modifying the original object. Not recorded automatically; must be inserted manually. Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.

args.name: JsonObject
args.desc: Name of the parameter that holds the JSON object handle returned by lr_eval_json.

args.name: Format
args.desc: Optional. Whitespace/line format: compact (no whitespace), indented (default, human-readable), or auto (compact in the Controller, indented in VuGen).

args.name: OutputParam
args.desc: Name of the parameter in which the resulting JSON string is stored.

name: lr_load_dll
description: Loads a DLL (Windows) or shared object (Linux) so that external functions can be called during replay with the C interpreter. A full path may be supplied. On Windows (non-SAP GUI), without a path the library is searched using the standard LoadLibrary order; SAP GUI requires a full path; on Linux, dlopen rules and LD_LIBRARY_PATH apply. Standard parameterization is not supported. Returns 0 on success, 10 if out of memory, and 11 if the file is not found.

args.name: library_name
args.desc: Name of the DLL (Windows) or shared object (Linux), optionally with a full path.

name: lr_log_message
description: Sends a message to the Vuser/agent log file rather than to the output window, which reduces network overhead during testing. Logging must be enabled in Runtime Settings with the "Always send messages" option. Returns the message length on success, or a negative number on failure.

args.name: format
args.desc: printf-style format string sent to the log file.

args.name: exp1, exp2,..expn
args.desc: Expressions/variables to format and print.
